summary: The Skyway Code includes a chart for finding headwind and crosswind components. Resolve the wind speed against the angle between the runway and the wind direction: crosswind = speed x sin of the angle, headwind = speed x cos of the angle. Example from the chart: 20 kt at 60° to the runway gives a 17 kt crosswind and a 10 kt headwind. Know the crosswind limit for your aircraft and confidence level. Built from the Skyway Code p.153 and pre-flight guidance on p.40.
src: The Skyway Code (CAP 1535 v4, Nov 2023), p.153
sections: Angle = angle between runway direction and wind direction
Crosswind = wind speed x sin(angle). Headwind = wind speed x cos(angle)
Chart example: 20 kt at 60° gives a crosswind of about 17 kt and a headwind of 10 kt
Rules of thumb: 30° gives about half the speed as crosswind, 45° about 70%, 60° about 85%, 90° all of it
If the wind comes from behind the runway direction (more than 90°) the headwind becomes a tailwind component
If significant crosswind is expected be confident in the technique, or practise with an instructor
Winds above about 35 kt aloft often mean bumpy conditions and strong headwinds raise fuel needs
Tailwind of 10% of lift-off speed increases take-off and landing distances by about x1.2

sum.Finding the components: Sine for crosswind, cosine for headwind.
sum.Using it: Practise technique and allow for tailwind effects.
